  <name>Task 1: Repair the StateExportService spec's dependency-injection setup and stale version assertion</name>

  <files>src/app/services/state-export.service.spec.ts</files>

  <read_first>
    - src/app/services/state-export.service.spec.ts (the file being modified — read in full; it is 201 lines)
    - src/app/services/state-export.service.ts (constructor at lines 44-51 lists the six real dependencies; `validateAndApplyState` at lines 333-407 shows which methods the import path calls)
    - src/app/services/model-attachment-defaults.service.spec.ts lines 60-100 (the established IndexedDBUserModelService spy pattern to copy verbatim — spy props `initialized$: of(true)` and `userModels$: of([])`)
    - src/app/services/state-management.service.ts lines 336-350 (confirms `setRestoringState` and `resetState` are real methods)
    - .planning/phases/02-service-architecture-serialization-safety/02-PATTERNS.md section "src/app/services/state-export.service.spec.ts"
  </read_first>

  <action>
Repair four specific defects in the spec's `beforeEach` and assertions. Do not restructure the file, do not rename existing `it()` blocks, and do not add fixture data — that belongs to plan 02-04.

Defect 1 — wrong service mocked (SERL-03 prerequisite). The spec imports and provides `UserModelService` from `./user-model.service`, but `StateExportService` injects `IndexedDBUserModelService` from `./indexeddb-user-model.service`. Because that service is `providedIn: 'root'`, TestBed silently constructs the real one and the spy has zero effect. Replace the import, the `mockUserModelService` declaration type, the `jasmine.createSpyObj` call, the `providers` entry, and the `TestBed.inject` cast so all five reference `IndexedDBUserModelService`. Create the spy with method list `getAllUserModels`, `saveUserModel`, `updateUserModel` and the property bag `{ initialized$: of(true), userModels$: of([]) }`, matching `model-attachment-defaults.service.spec.ts`. Keep `getAllUserModels` returning an empty array. Make `saveUserModel` and `updateUserModel` return a resolved promise, because plan 02-04 will import fixtures containing `userModels` entries and the service awaits those calls.

Defect 2 — root cause of the `should validate state structure correctly` failure. The `jasmine.createSpyObj('StateManagementService', [...])` method list omits `setRestoringState`, which is the first statement inside `validateAndApplyState`'s try block. Calling a method absent from a spy object throws a TypeError, which the catch block converts into a rejected `Failed to apply imported state` error — that is why the assertion reports `Expected [object Promise] not to be rejected`. Add `setRestoringState` to the method list. Audit the rest of the list against every `this.stateManagementService.` call site in `state-export.service.ts` and add any other missing name you find, so the spy is complete rather than only complete enough for today's assertions.

Defect 3 — stale version literal. Line 123 asserts `expect(parsed.version).toBe('1.0.5')` while `CURRENT_VERSION` in `state-export.service.ts` is `'1.0.11'`. Change the expected literal to `'1.0.11'` and add a short comment above it noting the literal must track `CURRENT_VERSION` in `state-export.service.ts`. Do not export the private constant from the service; this repo's convention throughout this spec is inlined literals.

Defect 4 — two unmocked dependencies. `StateExportService` also injects `CategoryService` and `ModelAttachmentDefaultsService`, neither of which is provided, so both real services are constructed and reach IndexedDB during the spec run. Add `jasmine.createSpyObj` entries for both and register them in `providers`. `CategoryService` needs `getAllCustomCategories` returning an object with empty `modelCategories` and `attachmentCategories` arrays, and `loadCustomCategories` returning a resolved promise. `ModelAttachmentDefaultsService` needs `getAllDefaults` returning an empty object and `loadDefaults` returning undefined. This makes the suite hermetic, which plan 02-04's fixture imports depend on.

Import `of` from `rxjs` is already present at line 2; no other new imports beyond the `IndexedDBUserModelService`, `CategoryService`, and `ModelAttachmentDefaultsService` symbols. Remove the now-unused `./user-model.service` import.
  </action>

  </verify>

<task type="auto">
  <name>Task 2: Create category.service.spec.ts pinning cascade behaviour before the DEP-01 refactor</name>

  <files>src/app/services/category.service.spec.ts</files>

  <read_first>
    - src/app/services/category.service.ts (full file, 536 lines — pay attention to the constructor at 70-75, `initializeService`/`loadCategories` at 80-172, `renameCategory` at 318-362, `deleteCategory` at 367-394, `cascadeRenameCategory` at 399-429, `cascadeDeleteCategory` at 434-439, and the lazy lookup at 445-457)
    - src/app/services/native-indexeddb.service.ts (method signatures: `init` returns a Promise, `getAll`/`add`/`update`/`delete` return Observables)
    - src/app/services/indexeddb-config.ts (the `StoredCategory` shape and `USER_MODEL_DB_CONFIG`)
    - src/app/services/model-attachment-defaults.service.spec.ts lines 60-100 (TestBed + spy conventions to follow)
    - .planning/phases/02-service-architecture-serialization-safety/02-PATTERNS.md section "src/app/services/category.service.spec.ts (NEW)"
  </read_first>

  <action>
Create a new spec that pins the observable behaviour of the two cascade methods against the CURRENT implementation, so plan 02-03's dependency-injection refactor has a before/after safety net. This spec must pass both before and after that refactor — write it against public API only, never against the private lookup helper.

The critical wiring detail: register `IndexedDBUserModelService` as a TestBed provider with a jasmine spy. Today `CategoryService` reaches that service through a runtime injector lookup; after plan 02-03 it will reach it through constructor injection. Both resolve through the same TestBed injector, so a single provider entry serves both implementations. Do not reference the private lookup helper by name anywhere in the spec.

Spy setup. For `IndexedDBUserModelService`, use the method list `getAllUserModels`, `updateUserModel` with the property bag `{ initialized$: of(true), userModels$: of([]) }`. For `NativeIndexedDBService`, use the method list `init`, `getAll`, `add`, `update`, `delete`; `init` resolves a promise, `getAll` returns an rxjs `of(...)` of the seeded stored-category array, `add` and `update` echo their data argument back through `of(...)`, and `delete` returns `of(undefined)`.

Seed data. `getAll` must return one non-default stored category so `renameCategory` and `deleteCategory` can find it: id `custom-model-1`, name `Robots`, type `model`, isDefault false, sortOrder 1, with `createdAt`/`updatedAt` dates. `getAllUserModels` must return three ImageModel objects sharing the category name `Robots` but with differing `type` values — one `custom_model`, one `model`, and one `custom_attachment` — so the type-discrimination branch at `category.service.ts:415-419` is genuinely exercised rather than assumed.

Cover four behaviours, each as its own `it()` inside named `describe` blocks matching the method under test:

First, service construction: `TestBed.inject(CategoryService)` returns a truthy instance and construction does not throw. This is the assertion that will detect a cyclic-injection regression after plan 02-03.

Second, `renameCategory` cascade to matching models: after awaiting `renameCategory('custom-model-1', 'Mechs')`, `updateUserModel` was called for each of the two model-typed entries with a second argument whose `category` is `Mechs`.

Third, `renameCategory` type discrimination: the same call did NOT invoke `updateUserModel` for the `custom_attachment`-typed entry, even though it shares the `Robots` category name. Assert on the exact call count and on the ids passed.

Fourth, `deleteCategory` reassignment: after awaiting `deleteCategory('custom-model-1')`, `updateUserModel` was called for the model-typed entries with a `category` of `Custom`, and `delete` was called on the native database spy with the store name and `custom-model-1`.

Follow the file's sibling conventions: two-space indent, single quotes, `describe('CategoryService', ...)` as the outer block, spies created inside `beforeEach`, and `TestBed.inject(...)` casts to `jasmine.SpyObj<...>` for anything the assertions read back.
  </action>
